```{r set-directories}
res_dir <- "../results/s07_ROH/"
```

# Load gt

```{r}
malagasy <-
  gt_load("../data/intermediate/rbind_data/malagasy_merge_clean_no_maf_1st_degree.gt")
```

This script is for the analysis of runs of homozygosity (ROH) in the
Malagasy population, using the Malagasy only dataset containing
`r nrow(malagasy)` individuals and `r ncol(malagasy)` loci.

```{r echo = FALSE}
testthat::expect_true(is_loci_table_ordered(malagasy, error_on_false = FALSE))
```

```{r echo = FALSE}
# malagasy <- gt_impute_simple(malagasy, method = "random")
```

# Examine SNP density in our dataset

```{r}
density <- show_loci(malagasy) %>%
  group_by(chromosome, window = floor(position / 1000)) %>% # per Kb
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop")

min_snp_coverage <- min(density$n)
cat("Minimum SNP coverage: ", min_snp_coverage, "\n")
median_snp_coverage <- median(density$n)
cat("Median SNP coverage: ", median_snp_coverage, "\n")
mean_snp_coverage <- mean(density$n)
cat("Mean SNP coverage: ", mean_snp_coverage, "\n")
```

# Set up parameters

```{r}
window_size <- 50 # size of window in SNPs, average SNP coverage is 1 per Kb, so this is approx 50Kb
threshold <- 0.05 #
min_snp <- 50 # min n. SNPs per run, average SNP coverage is 1 per Kb, so this is approx 50Kb
heterozygosity <- FALSE
max_opp_window <- 1 # n. of heterozygous SNPs permitted per run
max_miss_window <- 5 # max number of missing permitted
max_gap <- 100000 # max distance between SNPs in BP to be a run
min_length_bps <- 500000 # minimum length in BP of a run, 500kb
min_density <- 0.02 # minimum n. of SNP per kbps, roughly 1 SNP per 50kb
```

`windows_indiv_roh` uses a sliding window method to identify runs of
homozygosity. Window size was set to `r window_size` SNPs (approximately
`r window_size * median_snp_coverage` considering median SNP density in
the Malagasy dataset). This is the upper window limit tested by
[@pemberton2012]. Minimum length of runs was set to `r min_length_bps`
BPs, with a maximum distance of `r max_gap` between successive SNPs in a
window and a minimum SNP density of `r min_density` per kilobase. Within
each window, the thresholds for number of missing SNPs was set to
`r max_miss_window` and the maximum number of heterozygous SNPs
permitted was set to `r max_opp_window`. These parameters were chosen to
match the methods of [@kirin2010].

```{r message = FALSE}
malagasy <- malagasy %>% group_by(population)
runs <- windows_indiv_roh(malagasy,
  window_size = window_size,
  threshold = threshold,
  min_snp = min_snp,
  heterozygosity = heterozygosity,
  max_opp_window = max_opp_window,
  max_miss_window = max_miss_window,
  max_gap = max_gap,
  min_length_bps = min_length_bps,
  min_density = min_density
)
```

```{r}
# Load fastmixture Q matrix
qmats <- readRDS("../data/intermediate/fastmixture/fastmixture_m.RData")
mad_bor_g1000_sum <-
  gt_load("../data/intermediate/rbind_data/mad_bor_g1000_sum_clean.gt")
# subset to only malagasy
all_malagasy <- c(
  "Betsimisaraka", "Merina", "Sakalava_Tsimihety",
  "Betsileo", "Diego", "Vezo", "Mikea", "Temoro"
)
# tidy with the gt
tidyq <- augment(get_q_matrix(qmats, k = 3, run = 1), data = mad_bor_g1000_sum)
malagasyq <- tidyq %>% filter(population %in% all_malagasy)
# subset the malagasyq dataframe to only the "Merina"
merina <- malagasyq %>% filter(population == "Merina")
# group the merina
merina$group <- ifelse(merina$.Q2 < 0.5, "Social group A", "Social group B")
merinaA <- merina %>% filter(group == "Social group A")
merinaB <- merina %>% filter(group == "Social group B")

# match the runs$Individual and malagasy$id
matches <- match(runs$id, malagasy$id)
# add $population to runs
runs$Population <- malagasy$population[matches]
runs$Population <- as.character(malagasy$population[matches])
# if $Individual is in merinaA$id, add "merina_a" to runs$Population
runs$Population <- ifelse(runs$id %in% merinaA$id, "Merina_A", runs$Population)
# if $Individual is in merinaB$id, add "merina_b" to runs$Population
runs$Population <- ifelse(runs$id %in% merinaB$id, "Merina_B", runs$Population)
head(runs)
```

# Classify the runs

A Gaussian mixture-model from the package mclust [@scrucca2023] was then
used to classify runs into categories by length. Similarly to the
methods of [@pemberton2012], a range of 2 to 10 clusters were
investigated, and BIC was used to find the optimum number of clusters
through the clustCombiOptim function.

See <https://rdrr.io/cran/mclust/man/clustCombi.html> for details.

This method is similar to GARLIC [@szpiech2017], used by [@korunes2022],
which uses a Gaussian mixture model to classify runs into 3 categories
of small, medium, and long. Importantly, when GARLIC clusters runs
across populations, the Gaussian mixed-model alters the thresholds
classification of runs - so that in one population the threshold for a
'short' run will differ from the threshold in another population.
However, with mclust the thresholds are fixed across populations, so
that a 'short' run in one population is equivalent to a 'short' run in
another population.

```{r}
G <- 2:10
BIC <- mclust::mclustBIC(data = runs$lengthBps, G = G, modelNames = "V")
plot(BIC) # shows BIC values for G 1:10, plateaux at 3 clusters
summary(BIC)

classes_optimum <- mclust::Mclust(
  data = runs$lengthBps,
  G = 1:10, modelNames = "V"
)

clust_classes <- clustCombi(object = classes_optimum, data = runs$lengthBps) #

optimum <- clustCombiOptim(clust_classes) # returns optimum number of clusters
optimum$numClusters.combi
```

```{r}
classes <- mclust::Mclust(
  data = runs$lengthBps,
  G = optimum$numClusters.combi
) # creates the model
runs$classification <- as.factor(classes$classification)
classes$BIC # BIC values for the model, when given G
classes$parameters # gives details of each class
```

```{r}
ggplot(runs, aes(x = lengthBps / 1000000, fill = classification)) +
  geom_density() +
  labs(x = "Length of run (Mb)", y = "Density", fill = "Classification")
```

Clear differences are observed between individuals and ethnic groups in
the number and length of runs of homozygosity. Several factors explain
this pattern:

1)  The African component of Malagasy ancestry will be likely to have
    fewer ROH's, as African populations have lower homozygosity than
    other global pops, which introduces variation between individuals
    based on their proportion of African ancestry.

2)  IBD analysis (Alva et al 2022) suggests a bottleneck in the Asian
    ancestry source of all Malagasy people, meaning (if all other things
    were equal) the Asian ancestry component would have more ROH's than
    the African component

# Kruskal Wallis test

```{r}
kruskal.test(length ~ population, data = malagasy)
```

# Wilcox test

```{r}
pairwise.wilcox.test(malagasy$length, malagasy$population, p.adjust.method = "bonferroni")
```

To see how much ancestry is related to runs of homozygosity, we can plot
correlations of ROH versus ancestry for all individuals.

```{r}

mad_bor_g1000_sum <-
  gt_load("../data/intermediate/rbind_data/mad_bor_g1000_sum_clean.gt")
```


```{r}

  "Betsimisaraka", "Merina", "Sakalava_Tsimihety",

)
```

# Comparing proportion to ROH's

```{r}
malagasy_all <- malagasyq

# match
matching_m <- match(malagasyq$id, malagasy$id)
malagasy_all$n <- "NA"
malagasy_all$length <- "NA"
malagasy_all$mean <- "NA"
malagasy_all$n <- ifelse(!is.na(matching_m), malagasy$n[matching_m], malagasy_all$n)
malagasy_all$length <- ifelse(!is.na(matching_m), malagasy$length[matching_m], malagasy_all$length)
malagasy_all$mean <- ifelse(!is.na(matching_m), malagasy$mean[matching_m], malagasy_all$mean)
malagasy_all$median <- ifelse(!is.na(matching_m), malagasy$median[matching_m], malagasy_all$median)
head(malagasy_all)
```

Two Vezo individuals are clear outliers in the above plot. If we remove
these individuals what happens?

```{r}
nrow(malagasy_all)
malagasy_all <- malagasy_all %>% filter(mean < 2000000)
nrow(malagasy_all)
```

```{r}
ggplot(malagasy_all, aes(
  x = .Q2, y = mean / 1000000, fill = population,
  colour = population, shape = population
)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  labs(
    title = "Runs of homozygosity against ancestry proportion for Malagasy individuals",
    x = ".Q2 proportion (% African ancestry)", y = "Mean length of Runs (Mb)"
  ) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 3, 4, 8)) +
  theme(axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank()) +
  # axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +

    colour = guide_legend(title = "Population"),

  )

)
```
